messages.subject: Re: install without root?
messages.body_plain:
Hello Jake,

We have confirmed that their is a general problem with non-root installs and we will be working on a fix for this issue.

For the time being, you will need to either install the software as the root user or a user with 'sudo' privileges, that is listed
in the sudoers file.

Here is more information on setting up the 'sudoers' file:
https://www.linux.com/component/content/article/133-general-linux/397711

We hope to have this problem fixed in our next release, which will be in late January of 2016.

Stephen Weller
Revolution R Open Support Engineer

messages.subject: failed to increase the number of threads
messages.subject_clean: failed to increase the number of threads
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have installed Revolution R Open 3.2.2 and Math Kernel Library. MKL detects only 1 core (I have 18 cores). If I try to increase the number of threads with setMKLthreads() , I have this message :

> setMKLthreads(5)

Number of threads at maximum: no change has been made.

The detectCores() function from parallel library detects correctly available cores on my machine :

> detectCores()
[1] 18

My machine is a virtual machine running with xen.

Is the MKL library working on virtual machines or on physical machines only?

Thank you for your help.

Regards.

Vincent.

messages.subject: Re: failed to increase the number of threads
messages.subject_clean: failed to increase the number of threads
messages.body_plain:
Yes, MKL works with virtual machines (we do much of our testing on VMware and Hyper-V), but it defaults to using 1 thread per physical core; if your 18 virtual cores are simply threads on a single physical core, you will see the behavior you describe. You can find more information here <https://software.intel.com/en-us/articles/intel-math-kernel-library-intel-mkl-intel-mkl-100-threading>.

Cheers,
Rich Calaway
Microsoft R Team
